description: §9.9 the second TASK family: an open PROJECT. Where 'site' hands the room one file and says what goes in it, this hands them a filesystem and says nothing about what to build. The bench grows to match the premise, because the old one could not keep it: names may carry folders (src/parser.py, 4 levels), the room holds 40 files instead of 20, and [DELETE: name] can remove one — the first tool in the apparatus that DESTROYS shared work, and the sharpest territory signal it has (deleting someone else's file is a claim about whose project this is; fileWork's refactored matrix already counts who removes whose lines, and now counts who removes whose files). completion.target is '*': the agreement is about the whole tree, so any write or deletion anywhere lapses it. fileViewTotalChars caps the shared-file block at 80k so a 40-file room does not put its entire filesystem in every seat's prompt every turn — past the budget files are still LISTED with their sizes, never silently dropped. What this asks: with no deliverable named, does a room of six models converge on ONE project or fork into several? Who lays down the structure (the first mkdir-shaped write is architecture, and architecture is a role nobody assigned)? Does anyone delete, and whose? Read alongside 'site': same task-room machinery, one file vs a tree. NOT length-comparable with chat conditions (see §2.7); exploratory, out of registered stats.
welcomeMessage: Welcome to the room. You are each a different AI model. You will be here together for a while, and there is a shared filesystem: files everyone can read, change and remove. Make something in it, together. What that is — a program, a document, a library, something with no name yet — is yours to decide. There is no facilitator after this message. You can change anything here, including what the others have written. It is finished when you agree it is.
